newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-LEADING WOMEN IN THE AUSTRALIAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-LEADING WOMEN IN THE AUSTRALIAN OPEN.

text.p: Portraits of the leading women players in the Australian Open starting on Monday:

The undisputed queen of women's tennis, Graf has won the last six grand slam events she has played in, including three in 1996. The 27-old-German missed last year's Australian Open because of surgery on her left foot. Fit and well, she has been in a class over her own over the past year, despite the stress of her father's trial on tax avoidance charges. She has 21 grand slam titles and this year stands to pass Margaret Court's all-time record of 24 grand slam singles titles.
Seeding: 1. Age: 27. Weight: 59kg. Height: 1.75m. Ranking: 1. Tournament wins: 102. First round opponent: Janette Husarova (Slovakia)

She epitomises the never-say-die spirit, but has often fallen at the last hurdle to Graf or Monica Seles. She lost last year's Roland Garros and Wimbledon finals to Graf. A fierce competitor, Sanchez Vicario last tasted grand slam success in 1994 when she won the U.S. and French Opens. She has career earnings of $11,643,576 (behind Graf and Martina Navratilova).
Seeding: 2. Age: 25. Weight: 56kg. Height: 1.69m. Ranking: 3. Tournament wins: 24. First round opponent: Gloria Pizzichini (Italy)

The most exciting prospect in women's tennis since the emergence of Seles. Widely tipped to succeed Graf as number one and going on her present form could easily fulfil these expectations within the next two years. Her build-up to this tournament has been superb -- she has not lost a singles match this year in two tournaments. She shows remarkable maturity for a player only 16 years of age and last year showed she has the artillery to match her two higher-ranked contempories, beating both Graf and Seles. Hingis capped her year with a brilliant performance against Graf, losing an epic five-set final at the year-ending WTA championship. If she triumphs, Hingis will be the youngest grand slam winner.
Seeding: 4. Age: 16. Weight: 52kg. Height: 1.67m. Ranking: 4. Tournament wins: 3. First round opponent: Barbara Rittner (Germany)

Nearly always in contention around the quarter-finals, but invariably falters when the heat is on. Like Sanchez Vicario, rarely matches the likes of Seles and Graf, falling to both players in her only semifinal berths in grand slams last year. She has failed to live up to expectations after winning Wimbledon in 1994.
Seeding: 3. Age: 24. Weight: 59kg. Height: 1.70m. Ranking: 5. Tournament wins: 28. First round opponent: Miriam Oremans (Netherlands)

An outsider, but she has impressed many critics with her determined yet laid-back attitude in the second comeback of her career. She advanced to the semifinals at Roland Garros in 1990 at the age of 14 and enjoyed four years of top level tennis reaching a career-high ranking of six in the world before teenage burnout and well-publicised personal problems forced her from the game. She has started the year in fine style, reaching the final of the Sydney International at the weekend. Has jumped 13 places to 24 in the latest world rankings. A slow starter, she says fitness is her strength, which in a two-week grand slam event is essential.
Seeding: Unseeded. Age: 20. Weight: 61kg. Height: 1.74m. Ranking: 24. Tournament wins: 6. First round opponent: Jolene Watanabe (U.S.)
